clue.text: Backside mostly elegant and shocking

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so one letter is dropped from the reversed side

parts.note: split as back plus side: the word side read backwards
elegant means graceful

explanation.surface: Someone's rear end, almost stylish, is nonetheless outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backside' looks like one word for a bottom, but is read as 'side' turned round ('Back'), then cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shocking in the moral sense causes shame and scandal, a synonym pairing.

clue.text: Red activists get organised — that shows lots of guts!

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Left-wing campaigners getting their act together show great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage, the surface's sense, but is literal: the intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canals of the body are intestines, literally plenty of bowels.

clue.text: Shares making a comeback for single master

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pool is to share resources

explanation.surface: Stock prices rally for a lone boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' is a pun on 'mast': this boat has one mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sailing vessel with one mast is a single-masted craft.

clue.text: Will do the clue again?

definitions.meaning: will as in determination or a firm decision
to work out a puzzle once more

explanation.definitionFit: Determination is firmness of purpose; solving anew is a punning second reading.

clue.text: It will purge 1 down of muscly stereotypes

indicators.note: of means taken out from, so the letters come from within the next words

explanation.surface: Something designed to flush out stereotypes about muscle-bound people.
explanation.walkthrough: A clyster is an old word for an enema, which cleans out the bowels named at 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is an archaic purgative injected to clear the intestines.

clue.text: Writers were aware of extremes

parts.note: felt means sensed or were aware of
tips are the extreme ends of something

explanation.surface: Authors who were conscious of going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' seems to mean authors, but means pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Pens with fibrous points are instruments for writing with.

clue.text: Have no money left in bank account for trip

definitions.text: Have no money left in bank account
definitions.meaning: to be wiped out financially, with the account's sum gone
to trip is to stumble and fall

explanation.surface: Going broke is a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling means losing one's footing; financially it means losing what remains in an account.

clue.text: Toss rowers around shallow end — they aren't heavy

parts.note: to welter is to toss and roll about

indicators.note: the end of shallow is its final letter

parts.note: eights are rowing crews; around loosely says they sit next to the shallow letter

explanation.surface: Rowing crews thrashing about in the shallow end of a pool are not heavyweights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' only loosely places W next to the crews; WELTER is an old verb meaning to toss or roll about.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers in a middle weight class are lighter than heavyweights.

clue.text: One using needles to fix cut-up curtains

indicators.note: to fix means to mend or rearrange, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone sewing to repair damaged drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a seamstress; the needles are in fact the therapeutic kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of Chinese therapy inserts fine pins into the skin.

clue.text: Absorb European margins before tax

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its outer edges, so the first and last letters of European are taken

parts.note: a gross figure is the amount before tax is deducted

explanation.surface: An instruction to soak up the edges of Europe before paying duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone is to occupy their attention completely, a synonym pairing.

clue.text: For starters, Yoko Ono likes kippers — she also coddles some egg

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: A gossipy note on Yoko Ono's breakfast tastes: smoked fish and gently cooked eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow sac within an egg is one part of it, hence 'some egg'.

clue.text: Chuck Yeager maybe rewriting top titles

indicators.note: rewriting suggests the letters of top titles are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A famous aviator apparently revising the most important headings.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck Yeager was the American airman who first broke the sound barrier, flying experimental aircraft; 'maybe' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeager trialled new aircraft, making him an example of someone who flies prototypes for trials.

clue.text: Violent end met by destitute retreating soldiers

indicators.note: the end of Violent is its final letter
retreating means going backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: destitute means poor

explanation.surface: Fleeing soldiers, penniless, meet a brutal fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of soldiers, especially cavalry, is a collective noun for military personnel.

clue.text: They say command and control

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is spoken, a sound-alike rather than a spelling

parts.note: to reign is to rule or command

explanation.surface: Supposedly, giving orders and keeping things in check go together.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in check, as with a horse's straps, is to restrain or govern it.

clue.text: Petrel shot with 13 guns here!

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or broken up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is the word meaning control, a strap for a horse

explanation.surface: A seabird has been shot, and the guns are positioned right here.
explanation.walkthrough: A terreplein is the flat platform behind a rampart where cannon are mounted; the exclamation makes 'guns here' a description.
explanation.definitionFit: This fortification term names the level surface on which artillery stands, the place for cannon.

clue.text: After emergency exits cleared, head off to find visor

indicators.note: cleared means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters
off as in gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After fleeing a building, someone leaves to find a cap brim.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a peak shielding the face from glare, as this shade for the eyes does.

clue.text: All done at last, exactly what's needed

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of done

parts.note: the very thing is an idiom for exactly what is wanted

explanation.surface: A job finally completed, and it's just right.
explanation.definitionFit: All and its synonym both mean the whole lot, every item without exception.

clue.text: Keep exclusively clean rubbish!

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to oneself
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: An instruction to hoard the clean laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless talk is commonly called rubbish.

clue.text: New revolutionary cause to embrace new subtle differences

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold within
revolutionary means turning over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N again abbreviates new

explanation.surface: A fresh radical movement taking up a novel idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' anagrams CAUSE to UACES; 'to embrace' puts the second N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight shades of meaning or tone are fine distinctions.

clue.text: Help gambler to choose the odds

indicators.note: meant as picking alternate letters, though in fact the even-placed letters are kept and the odd ones dropped

explanation.surface: A punter seeks assistance in picking a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter later admitted the slip: the letters kept are the even ones, so 'ignore the odds' was intended.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone, often in wrongdoing, as in the legal phrase aid and assist.

clue.text: Sticks and leaves covering rooftop

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps around another

parts.note: leaves means goes, departs
the top of roof is its first letter

explanation.surface: Twigs and foliage blanket the top of a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' looks like a noun for twigs but is the verb: a bull sticks someone with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned animal piercing someone with its horns is said to impale or stab them that way.

clue.text: In prison camp almost come down with right kind of fever

indicators.note: in places the landing word within the shortened camp
almost means nearly whole, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a gulag is a Soviet prison camp
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: An inmate in a labour camp nearly falls ill with a particular fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Glandular fever is the British name for mononucleosis (mono).
explanation.definitionFit: Glandular fever is a viral illness, so the adjective names one type of feverish disease.

clue.text: One of 24 doing somersaults

indicators.note: somersaults means tumbling over, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dog performing acrobatic tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is the clue for dogs; this wild Australian dog is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild Australian dog belongs to the dog family named at 24.

clue.text: Cats love playing a bit of music

indicators.note: playing suggests the pieces are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: cats taken as two of a cat, giving the word twice
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Felines adore having fun with a scrap of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' is plural, so it supplies CAT twice; with O these are rearranged by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, a short musical composition.

clue.text: Publican in Essex keeps dogs

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A landlord in an English county breeds hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the dog family are classed together by zoologists by that group name.

clue.text: Manage to follow street code with a listening device

indicators.note: to follow places the managing word after the street and code pieces

parts.note: an ethos is a code of values
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Getting by while obeying highway rules, with the help of a hearing gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor uses this instrument to hear heart and lungs, an auscultation tool.
